Low-ratio m13 and m96 rows remain near ordinary behavior while m13, m96, m114, m118, m125, m159, and m209 become much later or broader at stronger conditions. The m191, m146, m90, and m216 outcomes show that nitrogen-containing families deserve explicit testing rather than being treated as generic carbonyls. Loading remains unresolved: m177 and m125 show large endpoint changes across amount and volume, whereas several neutral controls do not. The new batch therefore emphasizes matched ratio curves for m96, m114, m95, m191, m72, and m211; loading contrasts for m206, m117, m125, m216, and m177-like regimes; and ordinary neutral or non-donor controls to constrain transfer.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several likely failure regions while preserving scientifically meaningful local comparisons. The m96 and m114 series map low-to-high PE thresholds, and the m95, m191, m72, m206, and m211 points test whether those thresholds generalize across carbonyl, nitrogen, donor, and heteroaromatic scaffolds. Matched loading contrasts are included where recent labels suggest endpoint-specific amount or volume effects. High-ratio m11, m146, m193, and m216 experiments probe nitrogen-containing regimes that have produced large errors, while m167, m184, m40, and m121 provide non-donor or central controls. Together these labels can improve representation of condition-response curvature, structural gating, V1/V2 endpoint asymmetry, and calibration across both rare tails and the central Row-distribution."}
